t: This is Vauxhall Gardens, now a public park in Kennington on the south bank of the Thames, roughly opposite Tate Britain. It was once a famous pleasure garden, known as New Spring Gardens, which opened in 1661. Jonathan Tyers, who lived from 1702 to 1767, was its proprietor, and he owned the place. So the quiet park around you grew from a popular place of entertainment that he ran.
